rule: Every slide title is one SVOM sentence: subject, verb, object, so-what (the measure). The rule is mandatory.
Every slide follows data, analysis, insight, so what, takeaway.
The deck is key slides backed by data; each key slide can have detail slides behind it.
Build slides in slide format first (DeckCraft), so every slide fits a slide, then move to HTML.
Use callouts to draw the eye and takeaways; the whole must not be wordy.
Every chart has a title and units.
Comparisons keep parallelism: the same measure, the same base, the same order, for each item compared.
Always give the number, the quantity and the share of the total, and how they relate.
The answer is not necessarily yes or no; show the tradeoffs and the considerations behind each option.
Falsify every claim: name the least data that disproves it; do not recommend on an unvalidated trend.
Test criteria come from McKinsey and BCG primary material, not from one secondary source.
No 'xxxx: yyyy' titles; go straight to the message; adopt the key message and detail arrangement.
Titles are not wordy: at most two lines.
Answer-first executive summary; each block's bullets are the titles of the slides that support it, word for word. Reading only the titles tells the story.
No figure or assumption from outside the data. Where data is missing, state the gap and ask.
ASD-STE100 style, no em dashes, no filler phrases.
The executive summary opens with a strategic goals block: the meeting goal, the main goal, and the subgoals. The period result comes second.
Say which period a figure describes (June, not the quarter average) and distinguish observed from modeled.
